# RdistNN

Version **0.1.4**. See
[NEWS](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/NEWS.md) for changes.

**RdistNN** estimates conditional treatment effects and regression
functions using distributional nearest-neighbor (DNN) weights. Choose
covariate profiles, fit local estimates, and inspect jackknife standard
errors, local support and tuning sensitivity. For causal estimation, you
supply nuisance predictions; the package constructs the adjusted signals
and performs local estimation.

[Get
started](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html)
· [Function
reference](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/index.html)
· [Stata companion](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN_stata)

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("pak")  # once
pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN")
```

This installs production `master`. R 4.1.0 or newer, Rcpp and a C++17
compiler are required: Rtools on Windows, Xcode command line tools on
macOS, or an R-compatible compiler on Linux. For plots, also install
`ggplot2`; dashboards can use `patchwork`.

For the version-pinned release, use
`pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN@v0.1.4")`.

For reproducible installation, retain the full source commit or checked
archive identity;
[RELEASING.md](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/blob/master/RELEASING.md)
explains candidate installation and historical pins. The historical
`v0.1.0` tag predates CLATE and the current shared reporting interface.
Retain the source commit or archive identity alongside your results.

## Choose a workflow

| Goal | Function | Main inputs |
|----|----|----|
| Conditional average treatment effects | [`cate_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/cate_dnn.md) | Outcome, treatment and supplied outcome/propensity predictions, or a supplied pseudo-outcome |
| Conditional mean regression | [`np_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/np_dnn.md) | Outcome and covariates |
| Conditional effects among compliers | [`clate_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_dnn.md) | Outcome, binary treatment/instrument and instrument-arm nuisance predictions |
| Ratio of two local means | [`affine_ratio_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/affine_ratio_dnn.md) | Two aligned signals |
| Two-scale regression | [`np_tdnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/np_tdnn.md) | Outcome and two localization orders |
| Reusable DNN weights | [`weights_matrix()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_matrix.md) | Covariates and target profiles |

The estimators accept numeric matrices/vectors or data frames, including
tibbles. Select localization columns with `x_cols`; use `x0` for one
profile or `X0` for a matrix with one profile per row.

## A first CATE fit

This simulated example uses **oracle nuisance values**. In an
application, replace them with aligned predictions of the control
outcome mean, treated outcome mean and treatment propensity. RdistNN
does not fit those models.

``` r

library(RdistNN)

demo <- cate_demo_data(n = 180, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 1)
d <- demo$data
profiles <- cbind(X1 = seq(-0.5, 0.5, length.out = 5), X2 = 0)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = d, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y", t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle", m1_col = "m1_oracle", e_col = "e_oracle",
  X0 = profiles, k = 1L, return = c("W", "dx", "nuisance")
)
summary(fit_cate)$coefficients
#>           estimate std.error statistic      p.value    conf.low conf.high
#> target_1 0.1661760 0.2237942 0.7425393 4.577606e-01 -0.27245262 0.6048047
#> target_2 0.2282292 0.3240950 0.7042047 4.813053e-01 -0.40698531 0.8634437
#> target_3 0.4527139 0.2606611 1.7367908 8.242410e-02 -0.05817257 0.9636003
#> target_4 0.8600529 0.1748240 4.9195372 8.674907e-07  0.51740429 1.2027016
#> target_5 1.2093925 0.1633303 7.4045833 1.315629e-13  0.88927104 1.5295139
```

Each row reports the effect at one profile, its standard error and
pointwise confidence bounds. Inspect local support before interpreting a
profile:

``` r

as.data.frame(diagnostics(fit_cate))[, c("target_id", "n_eff", "treated_mass", "control_mass")]
#>          target_id    n_eff treated_mass control_mass
#> target_1  target_1 17.52493    0.4771771    0.5228229
#> target_2  target_2 17.52493    0.5726329    0.4273671
#> target_3  target_3 17.52493    0.7317029    0.2682971
#> target_4  target_4 17.52493    0.7015676    0.2984324
#> target_5  target_5 17.52493    0.6204591    0.3795409
```

With ggplot2 installed, the same fit gives a profile plot:

``` r

plot(fit_cate)
```

![CATE estimates at five X1 profiles with X2 fixed at zero, with
pointwise confidence
intervals.](reference/figures/README-cate-profile-1.png)

The [getting-started
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html)
shows matrix inputs, supplied signals and covariance between
prespecified profiles. Earlier `m_col` calls should use both arm means
for AIPW or a supplied `pseudo_outcome`; a pooled outcome mean is not a
substitute. The [migration
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html#migrating-earlier-cate-inputs)
describes the current signal inputs and refitting older development
objects. Fits report `meta$signal_source` and retain their original
`meta$created_with_version`; these describe the fit rather than certify
its inference assumptions.

## Regression and conditional LATE

For a conditional mean, reuse the same covariates and targets without
nuisance inputs:

``` r

fit_np <- np_dnn(data = d, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"), y_col = "Y", X0 = profiles)
data.frame(estimate = coef(fit_np))
#>           estimate
#> target_1 0.8244906
#> target_2 1.2066100
#> target_3 1.4750873
#> target_4 1.7033563
#> target_5 1.8859881
```

Use
[`clate_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_dnn.md)
for conditional LATE with a binary instrument and treatment. Supply the
instrument propensity and the outcome/treatment means in each instrument
arm. The [CLATE
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/conditional-late.html)
provides a complete example and explains the first-stage and status
outputs. Inspect the first stage alongside the ratio; weak local first
stages can make Wald intervals unreliable.

## Reporting, plots and tuning

CATE, regression and CLATE share
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html),
[`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html),
[`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html),
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) and
[`diagnostics()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/diagnostics.md).
Saved-fit prediction evaluates new profiles using retained observations
and signals. CATE and NP/TDNN expose joint target covariance through
[`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html); CLATE reports paired
covariance for each target.

Use
[`plot_weights()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_weights.md)
for localization,
[`plot_overlap()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_overlap.md)
for treatment or instrument support, and
[`plot_tuning()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_tuning.md)
after a grid fit. See the [plotting
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/visualising-fits.html)
for retained-data requirements and dashboards. Saved objects retain
observation-level numeric data and inherit the data’s sharing
restrictions.

The default is exact DNN with `k = 1`. The order `s` controls
localization: larger `s` concentrates weight closer to the target. Set
`s` explicitly or use `tuning_mode = "grid"` for sensitivity
comparisons; grids do not select a preferred fit. Jackknife uncertainty
requires `s < n`. The [tuning
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/kernel-order-tuning.html)
explains the default rule and candidate fits.

## Interpreting inference

Intervals are **pointwise**. The framework assumes independent
observations; cluster and survey-design inference are not supplied. At
each target, observations with exactly equal represented distance under
the selected metric share the average of their assigned rank weights,
including every deletion’s surviving group. Nearby distances are not
merged. This includes different covariate profiles at equal distance;
individual weights, support and effective sample size can change.
Aligned row permutations preserve estimates and covariance up to
numerical precision. Refit saved objects created under an earlier tie
policy.

The paper assumes a continuous distance distribution, under which the
earlier and current rules agree almost surely. The package warns when
distance ties occur: inference for persistent distance ties is not
established. Averaging does not supply a uniform mean-squared-error
improvement.

Nuisance predictions must be aligned with the estimation observations.
Propensity clipping is numerical protection, not a remedy for poor
overlap. Diagnostics describe local support; they do not establish
validity. For the identification, nuisance-learning and localization
conditions and theoretical results, see the accompanying
[paper](https://jakobjuergens.com/research/#orthogonal-inference-conditional-z).
The package guides explain the corresponding inputs and outputs.

## Numerical behavior and engines

Eligible calculations use C++ automatically, with R implementations
available for engine comparisons and troubleshooting. The
[getting-started
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html#seeds-and-native-threads)
explains engine selection, native thread limits and RNG behavior. Native
execution errors stop the calculation; automatic fallback applies when a
native routine is unavailable.

Asymptotic Beta tables retain a known rounding limitation at extremely
small tail masses, including possible R/Stata support differences. See
the [weight
guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/dnn-weights.html#numerical-limits)
before interpreting calculations at those scales.

## Further reading and help

- [Notation and
  conventions](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/notation-and-conventions.html):
  arguments, shapes and result fields.
- [Diagnostics and
  reporting](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/diagnostics-reporting.html):
  support and uncertainty summaries.
- [Paper
  replication](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/paper-affine-replication.html):
  the study-specific bundle and saved evidence.
- PLQR, local IV-GMM and ratio confidence-set inversion remain
  **experimental**; use their dedicated reference pages.

Use `citation("RdistNN")` for references. Report problems through the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/issues) with a
minimal example and
[`sessionInfo()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/sessionInfo.html).
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
covers development and numerical-engine contracts. RdistNN is licensed
under GPL version 3 or later.

# Package index

## Package overview

- [`RdistNN-package`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/RdistNN-package.md)
  [`RdistNN`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/RdistNN-package.md)
  : RdistNN: DNN Estimation for Conditional Effects and Regression

## CATE and regression — estimators and weights

The main estimation workflows: conditional average treatment effects,
nonparametric regression, and their DNN weight builders.

- [`cate_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/cate_dnn.md)
  : CATE via DNN rank-weighted pseudo-outcome averaging
- [`np_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/np_dnn.md)
  : Nonparametric regression via DNN rank weights
- [`np_tdnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/np_tdnn.md)
  : Nonparametric regression via TDNN rank weights
- [`weights_matrix()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_matrix.md)
  : Compute weight matrix W via an arbitrary ranking + weight mapping
- [`weights_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_dnn.md)
  : DNN weights (choose method), distance-based ranking
- [`weights_dnn_exact()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_dnn_exact.md)
  : DNN weights (exact full-U), distance-based ranking
- [`weights_dnn_asymp()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_dnn_asymp.md)
  : DNN weights (asymptotic full-U), distance-based ranking

  : Wrap a function as a tuning spec

  : Is this a tuning spec?

  : Register a tuning spec under a name
- [`get_tuning()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/get_tuning.md)
  : Retrieve a registered tuning spec

## General CATE simulation tools

Synthetic benchmarks and Monte Carlo summaries. The conditional
Z-estimation paper uses the separate study-specific replication bundle.

- [`sim_cate_data()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_cate_data.md)
  : Draw one sample from a named CATE simulation DGP
- [`sim_cate_one_rep()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_cate_one_rep.md)
  : Run one replicate of CATE estimators
- [`sim_cate_run()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_cate_run.md)
  : Run the CATE simulation grid
- [`sim_cate_methods()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_cate_methods.md)
  : List available CATE simulation methods
- [`summarise_sim_results()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/summarise_sim_results.md)
  : Summarise raw per-replicate CATE simulation results

## Conditional LATE and paired ratios

Supported supplied-prediction binary-IV signals and paired ratios with
exact or asymptotic DNN weights. Shared reporting, candidate views and
plots, with frozen-score covariance, diagnostics and the documented
pointwise inference conditions.

- [`clate_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_dnn.md)
  : Conditional LATE from externally supplied nuisance predictions
- [`iv_augmented_signals()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/iv_augmented_signals.md)
  : Construct augmented reduced-form and first-stage signals
- [`affine_ratio_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/affine_ratio_dnn.md)
  : DNN inference for a ratio of two supplied signal averages
- [`coef(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`confint(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`summary(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`print(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`print(`*`<rdistnn_summary_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  [`predict(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rdistnn_affine_ratio_result.md)
  : Reporting and prediction for paired affine-ratio results
- [`diagnostics(`*`<rdistnn_affine_ratio_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_diagnostics.md)
  [`diagnostics(`*`<rdistnn_clate_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_diagnostics.md)
  : Paired component and first-stage diagnostics
- [`clate_demo_data()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/clate_demo_data.md)
  : Bounded endogenous-treatment data for conditional LATE examples

## Experimental — ratio confidence sets

Optional pointwise normal-reference inversion of paired moment
inequalities. This helper does not establish weak-instrument-uniform
coverage.

- [`ratio_confidence_set()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/ratio_confidence_set.md)
  [`print(`*`<rdistnn_ratio_confidence_sets>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/ratio_confidence_set.md)
  : Confidence sets for a ratio of paired component estimates

## Experimental — PLQR

Experimental moments and density-backed uncertainty at supplied
coefficients. The wrapper does not solve for local coefficients; APIs
and inference interfaces may change.

- [`plqr_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plqr_dnn.md)
  : PLQR local moment evaluation and direct coefficient inference via
  DNN rank weights (experimental)

- [`plqr_score_matrix()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plqr_score_matrix.md)
  : Observation-level orthogonal PLQR scores at a supplied coefficient
  (experimental)

- [`score_plqr_component()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_plqr_component.md)
  : PLQR diagnostic score (component \\j\\); pure score (no weights, no
  fitting) (experimental)

- [`plqr_demo_data()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plqr_demo_data.md)
  : Minimal PLQR demo data (oracle nuisances; no internal fitting)
  (experimental)

- [`plqr_demo_subsets()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plqr_demo_subsets.md)
  : Quick helper: sample a batch of subsets (for U-stat / localization
  experiments) (experimental)

- [`print(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/print.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Print a `rdistnn_plqr_result` object (experimental)

- [`print(`*`<rdistnn_summary_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/print.rdistnn_summary_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Print a `rdistnn_summary_plqr_result` (experimental)

- [`summary(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/summary.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Summarize a `rdistnn_plqr_result` (experimental)

- [`confint(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/confint.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Confidence intervals for `rdistnn_plqr_result` (experimental)

- [`coef(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/coef.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Extract coefficients from a `rdistnn_plqr_result` (experimental)

- [`vcov(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/vcov.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Variance-covariance matrices for `rdistnn_plqr_result` (experimental)

- [`predict(`*`<rdistnn_plqr_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/predict.rdistnn_plqr_result.md)
  :

  Predict from a `rdistnn_plqr_result` object at new targets
  (experimental)

- [`plot_conditioning()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_conditioning.md)
  : Plot local design conditioning for PLQR fits (experimental)

- [`plot_calibration()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_calibration.md)
  : Plot local quantile calibration for PLQR fits (experimental)

## Experimental — local IV-GMM (companion paper)

Experimental companion functionality for the GMM paper; API and theorem
alignment may change before that paper is released.

- [`gmm_dnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/gmm_dnn.md)
  : Local GMM estimation via DNN rank weights

- [`iv_demo_data()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/iv_demo_data.md)
  : Minimal IV-GMM demo data

- [`sim_iv_data()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_iv_data.md)
  : Draw one sample from a named IV-GMM simulation DGP

- [`sim_iv_one_rep()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_iv_one_rep.md)
  : Run one replicate of IV-GMM estimators

- [`sim_iv_run()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_iv_run.md)
  : Run the IV-GMM simulation grid

- [`sim_iv_methods()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/sim_iv_methods.md)
  : List available IV simulation methods

- [`summarise_iv_results()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/summarise_iv_results.md)
  : Summarise raw IV-GMM simulation results

- [`new_gmm_model()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/new_gmm_model.md)
  : Create a local GMM model object

- [`is_gmm_model()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/is_gmm_model.md)
  : Test whether an object is a GMM model

- [`gmm_model_dr_iv()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/gmm_model_dr_iv.md)
  : Doubly robust IV GMM model

- [`print(`*`<rdistnn_gmm_result>`*`)`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/print.rdistnn_gmm_result.md)
  :

  :

  Confidence intervals for `rdistnn_gmm_result`

## Developer API — scores (U-stat kernels)

Extension points for custom scores: S3 spec, helpers, generics,
registries, and built-in score topics.

- [`new_score()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/new_score.md)
  : Score specification (S3) for U-stat kernels

- [`score_setup()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_setup.md)
  : Set up score context (precomputation)

- [`score_order()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_order.md)
  :

  Resolve kernel order `s`

- [`score_eval()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_eval.md)
  : Evaluate kernel on one subset

- [`score_eval_batch()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_eval_batch.md)
  : Evaluate kernel on many subsets (R fast-path)

- [`as_score()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/as_score.md)
  : Coerce a plain function to a score (simple cases)

- [`is_score()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/is_score.md)
  :

  Is object a `rdistnn_ustat_score`?

- [`is_compiled()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/is_compiled.md)
  : Does a score carry compiled-score pointer metadata?

- [`register_score()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/register_score.md)
  : Register a score

- [`get_score()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/get_score.md)
  : Retrieve a registered score

- [`list_scores()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/list_scores.md)
  : List registered scores

- [`score_np_y()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_np_y.md)
  :

  Nonparametric regression **singleton** score from observed outcome
  \\Y\\ (order-1 pure score; no weights)

- [`score_cate_rho()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_cate_rho.md)
  : CATE score from a precomputed pseudo-outcome \\\rho\\ (pure score;
  no weights)

- [`score_diff_path()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/score_diff_path.md)
  : Build a modular differentiable path for a score

## Developer API — distances (rankers)

Extension points for custom distances: S3 spec, helpers, generics,
registries, and built-in distance constructors.

- [`new_distance()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/new_distance.md)
  : Construct a distance spec
- [`distance_eval()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_eval.md)
  : Evaluate a distance spec at a single target
- [`distance_eval_batch()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_eval_batch.md)
  : Evaluate a distance spec for many targets (batch)
- [`as_distance()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/as_distance.md)
  : Wrap a function as a distance spec
- [`is_distance()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/is_distance.md)
  : Is this a distance spec?
- [`register_distance()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/register_distance.md)
  : Register a distance spec under a name
- [`get_distance()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/get_distance.md)
  : Retrieve a registered distance spec
- [`distance_names()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_names.md)
  : List registered distances
- [`distance_l2()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_l2.md)
  : L2 distance spec (single and batched evaluation)
- [`distance_l1()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_l1.md)
  : L1 distance spec (single and batched evaluation)
- [`distance_l2_scaled()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_l2_scaled.md)
  : Scaled L2 distance spec (one-time setup + eval/batch)
- [`distance_l1_scaled()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_l1_scaled.md)
  : Scaled L1 distance spec (one-time setup + eval/batch)
- [`distance_mahalanobis()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/distance_mahalanobis.md)
  : Mahalanobis distance spec (with one-time factorization)

## Developer API — rank → weight mappings

Extension points for custom rank weights: S3 spec, evaluators, registry,
and the single-scale DNN rank-weight constructors.

- [`new_rank_weight()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/new_rank_weight.md)
  : Construct a rank-weight spec
- [`rank_weight_eval()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_eval.md)
  : Evaluate rank-weight for a single target
- [`rank_weight_eval_batch()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_eval_batch.md)
  : Evaluate rank-weight for many targets (batch)
- [`as_rank_weight()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/as_rank_weight.md)
  : Wrap a function as a rdistnn_rank_weight spec
- [`is_rank_weight()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/is_rank_weight.md)
  : Is this a rdistnn_rank_weight spec?
- [`register_rank_weight()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/register_rank_weight.md)
  : Register a rdistnn_rank_weight under a name
- [`get_rank_weight()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/get_rank_weight.md)
  : Retrieve a registered rdistnn_rank_weight
- [`rank_weight_names()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_names.md)
  : List registered rdistnn_rank_weight names
- [`rank_weight_dnn_exact()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_dnn_exact.md)
  : Rank-weight: DNN exact (full U, WOR)
- [`rank_weight_dnn_asymp()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_dnn_asymp.md)
  : Rank-weight: DNN asymptotic (full U, WOR)

## Advanced — TDNN and jackknife-paper infrastructure

Two-scale DNN estimation and the leave-one-out jackknife primitives
supporting the generalized U-statistics companion paper.

- [`weights_tdnn()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_tdnn.md)
  : TDNN weights (choose method, k = 1), distance-based ranking
- [`weights_tdnn_exact()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_tdnn_exact.md)
  : TDNN weights (exact, k = 1), distance-based ranking
- [`weights_tdnn_asymp()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/weights_tdnn_asymp.md)
  : TDNN weights (asymptotic, k = 1), distance-based ranking
- [`rank_weight_tdnn_exact()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_tdnn_exact.md)
  : Rank-weight spec: TDNN exact (Demirkaya two-scale DNN, k = 1)
- [`rank_weight_tdnn_asymp()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/rank_weight_tdnn_asymp.md)
  : Rank-weight spec: TDNN asymptotic (Demirkaya two-scale DNN, k = 1)
- [`plot_tdnn_scales()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/plot_tdnn_scales.md)
  : Plot the TDNN two-scale decomposition
- [`jackknife_fast_rank()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/jackknife_fast_rank.md)
  : Fast delete-one jackknife for rank-weighted functionals (auto C++
  when available, R fallback otherwise)
- [`jackknife_rank_full()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/jackknife_rank_full.md)
  : Generic rank-order delete-one jackknife (prefix/suffix engine)
- [`jackknife_slow_rank()`](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/jackknife_slow_rank.md)
  : Slow delete-one jackknife for rank-weighted L-stat rules (fixed
  ranks)
